title: Rabbi Chiyya of Vastanya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Taanit 9a relates that he, Rav Shmuel bar Idi and Rav Huna bar Manoach used to be before Rava. When Rava died, they came before Rav Papa. Whenever he told them a teaching that did not seem reasonable to them, they would signal to one another. Rav Papa was distressed, and in a dream he was made to read: “And I cut off the three shepherds.” The next day, when they took leave of him, he said to them, “Let the Rabbis go in peace.” Yuchasin wrote that they died. Hyman observes that the Gemara does not say that the dream was fulfilled. In Zevachim 112a: “Rabbi Chiyya of Yustinya said: With a Nasi’s goat”; Dikdukei Soferim reads of Vastinya, and it is a place-name.

notes.text: Rava is the first teacher who died; Rav Papa is the later teacher distressed by the pupils. Hyman’s rejection of Yuchasin’s death report is a negative observation about the narrative, not proof that the pupils survived. נשיא in the sacrifice context means a ruler, not the patriarchal office.

The consulted narrative begins in Taanit 9a and continues in 9b with the dream and the farewell. It explicitly distinguishes the deceased Rava from the distressed Rav Papa. Silence about fulfillment does not prove that the pupils survived. The exact Yuchasin and Dikdukei Soferim claims remain Hyman-attributed.
